summary.headline: India Pesticides Q1 FY27 revenue fell 9.2% YoY to INR 256 crore and EBITDA margin to 15.4%, on weak domestic Pretilachlor demand from erratic rains.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue declined 9.2% YoY to INR 256 crore, driven by a 13% volume decline partly offset by about 4% price gain, with domestic revenue down to INR 167 crore from INR 195 crore. Export revenue was stable at INR 89 crore (about 35% of sales). EBITDA fell to INR 39 crore (15.4% margin vs 18.4%) and PAT to INR 23 crore from INR 35 crore, hit by lower volumes, a one-time INR 2.5 crore export receivable write-off, about INR 6 crore higher job-work charges and higher fuel and employee costs. Management guided FY27 top-line to lower single-digit growth, with Q3 and Q4 expected to be better.

segments.name: Chemicals (technicals)
segments.commentary: Q1 FY27 revenue INR 181 crore. Pretilachlor, the key paddy herbicide, saw softer domestic demand due to irregular rainfall.

segments.name: Formulations
segments.commentary: Q1 FY27 revenue INR 72 crore. Supported by 10,200 MT capacity, 18-state sales network, 24 depots and over 370 sales staff.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 89 crore vs INR 87 crore YoY, about 35% of total. Presence in more than 35 countries.

segments.name: Hamirpur subsidiary (new)
segments.commentary: 2 of 10 blocks operational. Management guides INR 50-60 crore revenue this year and about INR 1,000 crore over 3-4 years at 8-10 blocks.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth guided at lower single digit, with Q3 and Q4 expected to be better.
EBITDA margin guided at about 15.5-16% sustainably for FY27; management aspires to 18% if conditions improve.
Hamirpur revenue guided at INR 50-60 crore this year (revised down from INR 70-80 crore earlier); INR 1,000 crore potential over 3-4 years.
EU technical equivalence for a fungicide expected to add INR 30-40 crore revenue, with sales from about November.
Inventory days expected to fall from about 200 to about 170 by Q3.
Capex about INR 100 crore per year across Sandila and Hamirpur, funded from internal accruals with no term loans.
capex_capacity: Capacity: 28,300 MT technical and about 10,200 MT formulation across Sandila, Hardoi and Dewa Road.
Hamirpur: 2 of 10 blocks operational; herbicide multipurpose block under construction and fungicide block to follow; 2 blocks added per year.
Capex of INR 70-100 crore per year at Hamirpur (INR 80-100 crore per year cited later) and INR 25-30 crore at Sandila.
New fungicide (China-imported, about 4,000-5,000 t imports, company targets at least 2,000 t) to be made at Sandila with INR 2-3 crore balancing equipment; price INR 500-600/kg.
demand_pricing: Volume down about 13% YoY and price up about 4%, per CFO.
Subdued paddy and crop protection demand due to erratic monsoon, with excess rain damaging crops and deficient rain delaying sowing.
Management says Chinese imports are priced much lower, intensifying competition.
Exports slightly ahead of last year's Q1; new approvals expected to lift export revenue.
EU approval: existing EU molecule business about INR 100 crore annually; additional INR 30-40 crore expected.

qa_highlights.question: Reason for lower operating margin despite good gross margin?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO cited a one-time INR 2.5 crore export receivable write-off and about INR 6 crore higher job-work charges for raw material conversion into intermediates, plus higher fuel cost.

qa_highlights.question: Is the higher job-work spend linked to inventory for the upcoming season?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Intermediates were built in anticipation of a strong Q1 herbicide season; they are expected to be consumed from Q3 as June sales fell.

qa_highlights.question: Hamirpur revenue expectation for FY27 and the capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Revised to about INR 50-60 crore this year. Capex is INR 70-100 crore per year at Hamirpur plus INR 25-30 crore at Sandila; the company says roughly INR 100 crore per year in total.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainable EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says 15.5% is sustainable and targets around 18% if the environment improves; at least 15-16% is the floor.

qa_highlights.question: Why are inventory and receivables up?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said receivables were stable at about 120 days; only inventory rose, from 170 to about 200 days, due to lower sales, and should fall to about 170 in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue and volume-price split, and FY27 top-line guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume fell about 13% and price rose about 4%. FY27 growth guided at lower single digit, with Q3 and Q4 better.

qa_highlights.question: EU approval timing and value?
qa_highlights.answer: Sales expected from about November after customers add the new source; INR 30-40 crore of additional annual revenue expected on an existing INR 100 crore base.

risks_watch: Erratic monsoon may keep paddy herbicide volumes (Pretilachlor) subdued into the next quarter.
Chinese import price competition on existing and new products.
Hamirpur execution timelines: management has cut FY27 revenue guidance to INR 50-60 crore; third and fourth blocks not yet built.
Inventory days elevated at about 200 with a target of 170 by Q3; intermediate stock tied to job-work spend.
Single-molecule dependence (Pretilachlor) and the company's own acknowledgement of a need to diversify.
The new fungicide is unnamed; size and pricing are management estimates.
summary.management_tone: Cautious on near-term demand, citing erratic rains and a subdued quarter, but confident on the long term. Management was specific on capex, blocks and margin targets, and evasive on naming the new China-imported fungicide.
